previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder, COPD, chronic pain from prior trauma, and hypertension, was admitted after being found unresponsive and intoxicated. He presented with hypotension and hypoxia, which improved with IV fluids and oxygen support. His condition was complicated by a high blood alcohol level, somnolence, and prior noncompliance with treatment. A chest X-ray showed chronic emphysematous changes and bibasilar atelectasis without acute pneumonia. He received one dose of levofloxacin in the emergency department but did not complete a full course. Due to agitation, he required Haldol and brief physical restraints. Despite plans to initiate detox and pursue a Section 35 hold, James insisted on leaving against medical advice. He was alert and ambulatory at discharge, with understanding of the risks, and was advised to seek follow-up care.
